options.B: Having friendly colleagues.

questions.stem: What is the possible reason for people on part-time contracts to be happier?

options.A: They can hop from job to job easily.
options.B: They can win recognition of their work.
options.C: They can better balance work and life.
options.D: They can take on more than one job.

optionsCn.A: 他们能轻松地换工作。
optionsCn.B: 他们的工作能得到认可。
optionsCn.C: 他们能更好地平衡工作与生活。
optionsCn.D: 他们能身兼多职。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Welcome to Workplace!
lines.cn: M：欢迎收听《职场》节目！

lines.t: M: And in today's program, we're looking at the results of two recently published surveys, which both deal with the same topic, happiness at work.
lines.cn: M：在今天的节目里，我们要看两份最近发布的调查结果，它们涉及同一个话题：工作中的幸福感。

lines.t: M: John, tell us about the first survey.
lines.cn: M：约翰，给我们讲讲第一份调查。

lines.t: F: Well, this was done by a human resources consultancy who interviewed more than 1,000 workers and established a top 10 of the factors which make people happy at work.
lines.cn: F：嗯，这份调查由一家人力资源咨询公司完成，他们访谈了 1000 多名员工，列出了让人在工作中感到快乐的前十大因素。

lines.t: F: The most important factor for the majority of the people interviewed was having friendly, supportive colleagues.
lines.cn: F：对大多数受访者来说，最重要的因素是有友好、能相互支持的同事。

lines.t: F: In fact, 73% of people interviewed put their relationship with colleagues as the key factor contributing to happiness at work, which is a very high percentage.
lines.cn: F：事实上，73% 的受访者把与同事的关系列为带来工作幸福感的关键因素，这个比例非常高。

lines.t: F: The second most important factor was having work that is enjoyable.
lines.cn: F：第二重要的因素是有令人愉快的工作内容。

lines.t: F: The two least important factors were having one's achievements recognised and, rather surprisingly, earning a competitive salary.
lines.cn: F：最不重要的两个因素是自己的成就得到认可，以及相当令人意外地，拿到有竞争力的薪水。

lines.t: M: So, we're not mainly motivated by money?
lines.cn: M：所以，我们的主要动力并不是金钱？

lines.t: F: Apparently not.
lines.cn: F：显然不是。

lines.t: M: Any other interesting information in the survey?
lines.cn: M：调查里还有其他有意思的信息吗？

lines.t: F: Yes. For example, 25% of the working people interviewed described themselves as very happy at work.
lines.cn: F：有。比如，受访的在职人士中有 25% 说自己工作时非常快乐。

lines.t: F: However, 20% of employees described themselves as being unhappy.
lines.cn: F：然而，有 20% 的员工说自己并不快乐。

lines.t: M: That's quite a lot of unhappy people at work every day.
lines.cn: M：那意味着每天有相当多的人工作得不开心。

lines.t: F: It is, isn't it?
lines.cn: F：的确如此，是不是？

lines.t: F: And there were several more interesting conclusions revealed by the survey.
lines.cn: F：调查还揭示了另外几个有意思的结论。

lines.t: F: First of all, small is beautiful.
lines.cn: F：首先，小即是美。

lines.t: F: People definitely prefer working for smaller organisations or companies with less than 100 staff.
lines.cn: F：人们肯定更愿意在规模较小的机构或员工不到 100 人的公司工作。

lines.t: F: We also find out that, generally speaking, women were happier in their work than men.
lines.cn: F：我们还发现，总体而言，女性在工作中比男性更快乐。

lines.t: F: Yes, we are, aren't we?
lines.cn: F：是啊，我们确实如此，对吧？

lines.t: F: And workers on part-time contracts, who only work 4 or 5 hours a day, are happier than those who work full-time.
lines.cn: F：而且每天只工作四五小时的兼职员工比全职员工更快乐。

lines.t: F: The researchers concluded that this is probably due to a better work-life balance.
lines.cn: F：研究者认为，这大概是因为他们更好地平衡了工作与生活。

lines.t: M: Are bosses happier than their employees?
lines.cn: M：老板比员工更快乐吗？

lines.t: F: Yes, perhaps not surprisingly.
lines.cn: F：是的，这也许并不让人意外。

lines.t: F: The higher people go in a company, the happier they are.
lines.cn: F：在公司里职位越高，人就越快乐。

lines.t: F: So senior managers enjoy their jobs more than people working under them.
lines.cn: F：所以高层管理者比在他们手下工作的人更享受自己的工作。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: Mr. DeKaiser, I'm a great lover of your book, Moments Before the Flood. Can you tell us how you first became interested in this subject matter?
lines.cn: F：德凯泽先生，我非常喜欢您的书《洪水之前》。您能讲讲最初是怎么对这个题材产生兴趣的吗？

lines.t: M: In 2006, when the concert hall of the city of Bruges asked me to take some pictures for a catalogue for a new concert season around the theme of water, I found myself working along the Belgian coastline.
lines.cn: M：2006 年，布鲁日市音乐厅请我为以“水”为主题的新演出季图册拍些照片，我就这样来到了比利时海岸线一带工作。

lines.t: M: As there had been numerous alarming articles in the press about a climate catastrophe waiting to happen, I started looking at the sea and the beach very differently, a place where I spent so many perfect days as a child.
lines.cn: M：由于报刊上有许多关于气候灾难即将降临的警示文章，我开始以完全不同的眼光看待大海和海滩——那是我童年度过无数美好时光的地方。

lines.t: M: This fear of a looming danger became the subject of a large-scale photo project.
lines.cn: M：这种对迫近危险的恐惧，成了一个大规模摄影项目的主题。

lines.t: M: It is clear now that it's a matter of time before the entire European coastline disappears under the water.
lines.cn: M：现在很清楚，整条欧洲海岸线沉入水下只是时间问题。

lines.t: M: The same goes for numerous big cities around the world.
lines.cn: M：世界上众多大城市也是如此。

lines.t: M: My idea was to photograph this beautiful and very unique coastline, rich in history, before it's too late. As a last witness.
lines.cn: M：我的想法是在还来得及的时候，为这条美丽独特、历史悠久的欧洲海岸线留下影像——作为一名最后的见证者。

lines.t: F: Can you talk a bit about how history plays a role in this project?
lines.cn: F：能谈谈历史在这个项目中起了什么作用吗？

lines.t: M: Sure, the project is also about the history of Europe looking at the sea and wondering when the next enemy would appear.
lines.cn: M：当然。这个项目也关乎欧洲的历史——它眺望大海，担心下一个敌人何时出现。

lines.t: M: In the images, you see all kinds of possible defense constructions to hold back the Romans, Germans, Vikings, and now nature as enemy number one.
lines.cn: M：在这些照片里，你能看到各种各样的防御工事，用来抵挡罗马人、日耳曼人、维京人，而如今头号敌人成了大自然。

lines.t: M: For example, there is the image of the bridge into the sea, taken at the Normandy D-Day landing site.
lines.cn: M：例如，有一张伸入海中的桥的照片，拍摄于诺曼底登陆地点。

lines.t: M: Also Venice, the city eternally threatened by the sea, where every morning wooden pathways have to be set up to allow tourists to reach their hotels.
lines.cn: M：还有威尼斯——这座永远受大海威胁的城市，每天早晨都必须架起木板通道，让游客能走到他们的酒店。

lines.t: F: Thank you Mr. DeKaiser. It was a pleasure to have you with us today.
lines.cn: F：谢谢您，德凯泽先生。今天很高兴能请您来。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: When facing a new situation, some people tend to rehearse their defeat by spending too much time anticipating the worst.
lines.cn: 面对新情况时，有些人会花太多时间预想最坏的结果，等于在预演自己的失败。

lines.t: I remember talking with a young lawyer who was about to begin her first jury trial.
lines.cn: 我记得曾和一位即将开始第一次陪审团审判的年轻律师交谈。

lines.t: She was very nervous.
lines.cn: 她非常紧张。

lines.t: I asked what impression she wanted to make on the jury.
lines.cn: 我问她想给陪审团留下什么印象。

lines.t: She replied, I don't want to look too inexperienced.
lines.cn: 她回答说：我不想看起来太没经验。

lines.t: I don't want them to suspect this is my first trial.
lines.cn: 我不想让他们怀疑这是我的第一次出庭。

lines.t: This lawyer had fallen victim to the don'ts syndrome, a form of negative goal setting.
lines.cn: 这位律师成了“不要”综合征的受害者，这是一种消极的目标设定。

lines.t: The don'ts can be self-fulfilling because your mind responds to pictures.
lines.cn: 这些“不要”可能自我应验，因为你的大脑会对画面作出反应。

lines.t: Research conducted at Stanford University shows a mental image fires the nervous system the same way as actually doing something.
lines.cn: 斯坦福大学进行的研究表明，心理意象激发神经系统的方式与实际做某件事时相同。

lines.t: That means when a golfer tells himself, don't hit the ball into the water.
lines.cn: 这意味着当高尔夫球手对自己说“别把球打进水里”时，

lines.t: His mind sees the image of the ball flying into the water.
lines.cn: 他脑中看到的却是球飞进水里的画面。

lines.t: So guess where the ball will go.
lines.cn: 所以猜猜球会飞向哪里。

lines.t: Consequently, before going into any stressful situation, focus only on what you want to have happen.
lines.cn: 因此，在进入任何有压力的情境之前，只把注意力放在你希望发生的事情上。

lines.t: I asked the lawyer again how she wanted to appear at her first trial and this time she said, I want to look professional and self-assured.
lines.cn: 我再次问那位律师想在第一次出庭时呈现出什么样子，这次她说：我想看起来专业而自信。

lines.t: I told her to create a picture of what self-assured would look like.
lines.cn: 我让她在心里描绘出“自信”是什么样子。

lines.t: To her, it meant moving confidently around the courtroom, using convincing body language and projecting her voice so it could be heard from the judge's bench to the back door.
lines.cn: 对她来说，那意味着在法庭上自信地走动，运用有说服力的肢体语言，并且把声音送出去，从法官席一直传到后门都能听见。

lines.t: She also imagined a skilful closing argument and a winning trial.
lines.cn: 她还想象了一场技巧娴熟的终结辩论和一场胜诉。

lines.t: A few weeks after this positive dress rehearsal, the young lawyer did win.
lines.cn: 在这次积极的心理彩排几周之后，这位年轻律师真的赢了。

optionsCn.A: 纤维可能有助于降低体内激素水平。
optionsCn.B: 纤维对女性的益处可能多于男性。
optionsCn.C: 纤维可能改善心肌功能。
optionsCn.D: 纤维可能使血液循环更顺畅。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: Most Americans don't eat enough fruits, vegetables or whole grains.
lines.cn: 大多数美国人吃的水果、蔬菜或全谷物都不够。

lines.t: Research now says adding fiber to the teen diet may help lower the risk of breast cancer.
lines.cn: 如今有研究指出，在青少年饮食中增加纤维可能有助于降低乳腺癌风险。

lines.t: Conversations about the benefits of fiber are probably more common in nursing homes than high schools.
lines.cn: 关于纤维益处的讨论，在养老院大概比在高中更常见。

lines.t: But along comes a new study that could change that.
lines.cn: 但一项新研究可能会改变这种情况。

lines.t: Christie King, a diet specialist at Texas Children's Hospital, finds it hard to get teenage patients' attention about healthy eating.
lines.cn: 德克萨斯儿童医院的饮食专家克里斯蒂·金发现，很难让青少年患者关注健康饮食。

lines.t: But telling them that eating lots of high fiber foods could reduce the risk of breast cancer before middle age, that's a powerful message.
lines.cn: 但告诉他们多吃高纤维食物可以降低中年之前患乳腺癌的风险，就很有说服力。

lines.t: The new finding is based on a study of 44,000 women.
lines.cn: 这一新发现基于一项对 4.4 万名女性的研究。

lines.t: They were surveyed about their diets during high school, and their eating habits were tracked for two decades.
lines.cn: 研究者调查了她们高中时期的饮食，并追踪了她们的饮食习惯长达二十年。

lines.t: It turns out that those who consumed the highest levels of fiber during adolescence had a lower risk of developing breast cancer compared to the women who ate the least fiber.
lines.cn: 结果显示，与摄入纤维最少的女性相比，青春期摄入纤维最多的女性患乳腺癌的风险更低。

lines.t: This important study demonstrates that the more fiber you eat during your high school years, the lower your risk is in developing breast cancer in later life.
lines.cn: 这项重要的研究表明，高中时期吃的纤维越多，日后患乳腺癌的风险就越低。

lines.t: The finding points to long-standing evidence that fiber may reduce circulating female hormone levels, which could explain the reduced risk.
lines.cn: 这一发现印证了长期以来的证据：纤维可能降低体内循环的女性激素水平，这或许能解释风险的下降。

lines.t: The bottom line here is the more fiber you eat, perhaps a lower level of hormone in your body, and therefore a lower lifetime risk of developing breast cancer.
lines.cn: 说到底就是：你吃的纤维越多，体内的激素水平可能越低，因此一生中患乳腺癌的风险也越低。

lines.t: High fiber diets are also linked to a reduced risk of heart disease and diabetes.
lines.cn: 高纤维饮食还与降低心脏病和糖尿病的风险有关。

lines.t: That's why women are told to eat 25 grams of fiber a day, men even more.
lines.cn: 这就是为什么建议女性每天摄入 25 克纤维，男性还要更多。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组

optionsCn.B: 它一年比一年严重。

questions.cn: 讲话者说他的学生去年做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们用一周时间研究自己的消费行为。
optionsCn.B: 他们研究了手机对年轻人的影响。
optionsCn.C: 他们分析了自家这些年的预算。
optionsCn.D: 他们对广告做了详尽的研究。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Well, my current research is really about consumer behaviour, so recently I've looked at young people's drinking and it's obviously a major concern to government at the moment.
lines.cn: 嗯，我目前的研究其实是关于消费者行为的，所以最近我研究了年轻人的饮酒问题，这显然是政府当前非常关注的事情。

lines.t: I've also looked at how older people are represented in the media.
lines.cn: 我也研究了老年人在媒体中的形象呈现。

lines.t: Again, it's of major current interest with older people becoming a much larger proportion of UK and indeed world society.
lines.cn: 这同样是当前的重要议题，因为老年人在英国乃至整个世界人口中所占比例越来越大。

lines.t: I'm also interested in how consumers operate online and how that online behaviour might be different from how they operate offline when they go to the shops.
lines.cn: 我还对消费者在网上的行为方式感兴趣，以及这种线上行为与他们去实体店购物时的线下行为可能有何不同。

lines.t: Well, I think that the important thing here is to actually understand what's happening from the consumer's perspective.
lines.cn: 嗯，我认为重要的是真正从消费者的角度去理解正在发生什么。

lines.t: One of the things that businesses and indeed government organisations often fail to do is to really see what is happening from the consumer's perspective.
lines.cn: 企业和政府机构常常未能做到的一件事，就是真正从消费者的角度看清正在发生什么。

lines.t: For example, in the case of young people's drinking, one of the things that I've identified is that drinking for people say between the ages of 18 and 24 is all about the social activity.
lines.cn: 例如，在年轻人饮酒的问题上，我发现的一点是：对 18 到 24 岁的人来说，喝酒完全是一种社交活动。

lines.t: A lot of the government advertising has been about individual responsibility but actually understanding that drinking is very much about the social activity and finding ways to help young people get home safely and not end up in hospital is one of the things that we've tried to present there.
lines.cn: 政府的许多宣传都在讲个人责任，但真正理解喝酒与社交活动的密切关系，并找到办法帮助年轻人安全回家、不至于进医院，才是我们一直试图推进的方向之一。

lines.t: The key thing about consumer behaviour is that it's very much about how consumers change.
lines.cn: 消费者行为的关键在于，它很大程度上关乎消费者如何变化。

lines.t: Markets always change faster than marketing, so we have to look at what consumers are doing.
lines.cn: 市场的变化总是快于营销，所以我们必须关注消费者在做什么。

lines.t: Currently I teach consumer behaviour to undergraduates in their second year and we look at all kinds of things in consumer behaviour and particularly how consumers are presented in advertising.
lines.cn: 目前我给大二本科生讲授消费者行为学，我们会研究消费者行为的方方面面，尤其是消费者在广告中是如何被呈现的。

lines.t: So they get involved by looking at advertising and really critically assessing the consumer behaviour aspects of it and getting involved sometimes doing primary research.
lines.cn: 所以他们会参与进来，审视广告，批判性地评估其中的消费者行为要素，有时还亲自做一手研究。

lines.t: For example, last year my students spent a week looking at their own purchasing and analysed it in detail from shopping to the relationship that they have with their retail banks and their mobile phone providers.
lines.cn: 例如，去年我的学生用一周时间观察自己的消费行为，并做了详细分析，从购物一直到他们与开户银行和手机运营商之间的关系。

lines.t: I think they found it very useful and it also helped them identify just what kind of budgets they had too.
lines.cn: 我想他们觉得这很有用，也帮他们弄清了自己的预算到底是什么状况。

lines.t: The fact of the matter is that there's a whole range of interesting research out there and I think as the years go on there's going to be much more for us to consider and certainly much more for students to become involved in.
lines.cn: 事实是，有一系列有趣的研究等着我们去做，而且我认为随着时间推移，会有更多内容值得我们思考，也肯定会有更多课题供学生参与。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Sweden was the first European country to print and use paper money.
lines.cn: 瑞典是第一个印制并使用纸币的欧洲国家。

lines.t: But it may soon do away with physical currencies.
lines.cn: 但它可能很快就会废除实体货币。

lines.t: Banks can save a lot of money and avoid regulatory headaches by moving to a cash-free system.
lines.cn: 转向无现金体系，银行可以省下大笔费用，也免去监管上的麻烦。

lines.t: And they can also avoid bank robberies, theft and dirty money.
lines.cn: 他们还能避免银行抢劫、盗窃和黑钱的问题。

lines.t: Claire Barrett, the editor of Financial Times Money, says the western world is headed toward a world without physical currency.
lines.cn: 《金融时报·理财》版编辑克莱尔·巴雷特说，西方世界正走向一个没有实体货币的世界。

lines.t: Andy Holder, the chief economist at the Bank of England, suggested that the UK move towards a government-backed digital currency.
lines.cn: 英格兰银行首席经济学家安迪·霍尔德建议英国转向由政府背书的数字货币。

lines.t: But does a cashless society really make good economic sense?
lines.cn: 但无现金社会真的在经济上说得通吗？

lines.t: The fact that cash is being drawn out of society is less a feature of our everyday lives and the ease of electronic payments.
lines.cn: 现金正被抽离出社会，这更多是电子支付日益便利的结果，而不太像我们日常生活本身的什么特征。

lines.t: Is this actually making us spend more money without realizing it?
lines.cn: 这是否实际上让我们在不知不觉中花了更多钱？

lines.t: Barrett wanted to find out if the absence of physical currency does indeed cause a person to spend more.
lines.cn: 巴雷特想弄清，没有实体货币是否真的会让人花更多钱。

lines.t: So she decided to conduct an experiment a few months ago.
lines.cn: 于是几个月前她决定做一项实验。

lines.t: She decided that she was going to try to just use cash for two weeks to make all of her essential purchases and see what that would do to her spending.
lines.cn: 她决定尝试在两周内只用现金完成所有必需品的购买，看看这会对她的花销产生什么影响。

lines.t: She found she did spend a lot less money because it is incredibly hard to predict how much cash one is going to need.
lines.cn: 她发现自己确实少花了很多钱，因为要预测需要多少现金实在太难了。

lines.t: She was forever drawing money out of cash points.
lines.cn: 她总是不停地从自动取款机里取钱。

lines.t: Months later she was still finding cash stuffed in her trouser pockets and the pockets of her handbags.
lines.cn: 几个月后，她还不断在裤兜和手提包口袋里发现塞着的现金。

lines.t: During the experiment Barrett took a train ride.
lines.cn: 实验期间，巴雷特坐了一趟火车。

lines.t: On the way there was an announcement that the restaurant car was not currently accepting credit cards.
lines.cn: 途中广播说，餐车目前不接受信用卡。

lines.t: The train cars were filled with groans because many of the passengers were traveling without cash.
lines.cn: 车厢里一片哀叹声，因为许多乘客出行时都没有带现金。

lines.t: It underlines just how much things have changed in the last generation, Barrett says.
lines.cn: 巴雷特说，这恰恰凸显出上一代到现在发生了多大的变化。

lines.t: My parents, when they were younger, used to budget by putting money into envelopes.
lines.cn: 我父母年轻时，习惯把钱装进信封来做预算。

lines.t: They'd get paid and they'd immediately separate the cash into piles and put them in envelopes so they knew what they had to spend week by week.
lines.cn: 一拿到工资，他们就把现金分成几堆装进信封，这样就知道每一周该花多少。

lines.t: It was a very effective way for them to keep track of their spending.
lines.cn: 对他们来说，这是掌握开支非常有效的办法。

lines.t: Nowadays we're all on credit cards, we're doing online purchases and money is kind of becoming a less physical and more imaginary type of thing that we can't get our hands around.
lines.cn: 如今我们都用信用卡、在网上购物，钱在某种程度上变得越来越不具实体、越来越虚，我们根本抓不住它。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Why should you consider taking a course in demography in college?
lines.cn: 你为什么应该考虑在大学里选修一门人口学课？

lines.t: You will be growing up in the generation where the baby boomers are going into retirement and dying.
lines.cn: 你将成长在婴儿潮一代逐渐退休并离世的那一代人之中。

lines.t: You will face problems in the aging of the population that have never been faced before.
lines.cn: 你将面对前所未有的人口老龄化问题。

lines.t: You will hear more and more about migration between countries and between rural areas and cities.
lines.cn: 你会越来越多地听到关于国家之间以及城乡之间人口迁移的话题。

lines.t: You need to understand as a citizen and as a taxpayer and as a voter what's really behind the arguments.
lines.cn: 作为公民、纳税人和选民，你需要理解这些争论背后真正的东西。

lines.t: I want to tell you about the past, present and future of the human population.
lines.cn: 我想和你们谈谈人类人口的过去、现在和未来。

lines.t: So let's start with a few problems.
lines.cn: 那我们就从几个问题谈起。

lines.t: Right now a billion people are chronically hungry.
lines.cn: 此刻就有十亿人长期处于饥饿之中。

lines.t: That means they wake up hungry, they're hungry all day and they go to sleep hungry.
lines.cn: 也就是说，他们饿着醒来，饿着过完一天，又饿着睡去。

lines.t: A billion people are living in slums. Not the same billion people, but there is some overlap.
lines.cn: 有十亿人住在贫民窟。这十亿人与前面那十亿并非同一批人，但有一部分重叠。

lines.t: Living in slums means they don't have infrastructure to take the garbage away.
lines.cn: 住在贫民窟意味着他们没有把垃圾运走的基础设施。

lines.t: They don't have secure water supplies to drink.
lines.cn: 他们没有稳定可靠的饮用水供应。

lines.t: Nearly a billion people are illiterate. Try to imagine your life being illiterate.
lines.cn: 近十亿人是文盲。试着想象一下不识字的生活。

lines.t: You can't read the labels on the bottles in the supermarket if you can get to a supermarket.
lines.cn: 就算你能进超市，也读不懂货架上瓶子的标签。

lines.t: Two thirds of those people who are illiterate are women and about 200 to 215 million women don't have access to birth control they want so that they can control their own fertility.
lines.cn: 这些文盲中有三分之二是女性，而大约 2 亿到 2.15 亿女性无法获得她们想要的避孕手段，从而自主掌控自己的生育。

lines.t: This is not only a problem in developing countries.
lines.cn: 这不仅是发展中国家的问题。

lines.t: About half of all pregnancies globally are unintended.
lines.cn: 全球所有怀孕中约有一半是非计划内的。

lines.t: So those are examples of population problems.
lines.cn: 以上就是人口问题的一些例子。

lines.t: Demography gives you the tools to understand and to address these problems.
lines.cn: 人口学为你提供理解和应对这些问题的工具。

lines.t: It's not only the study of human population but the populations of non-human species including viruses like influenza, the bacteria in your gut, plants that you eat, animals that you enjoy or that provide you with meat.
lines.cn: 它不仅研究人类人口，也研究非人类物种的种群，包括流感病毒、你肠道里的细菌、你吃的植物，以及你喜爱的或为你提供肉食的动物。

lines.t: Demography also includes the study of non-living objects like light bulbs and taxi cabs and buildings because these are also populations.
lines.cn: 人口学还包括对非生命对象的研究，比如灯泡、出租车和建筑物，因为它们也构成“种群”。

lines.t: It studies these populations in the past, present and future using quantitative data and mathematical models as tools of analysis.
lines.cn: 它运用定量数据和数学模型作为分析工具，研究这些种群在过去、现在与未来的状况。

lines.t: I see demography as a central subject related to economics.
lines.cn: 我认为人口学是一门与经济学相关的核心学科。

lines.t: It is the means to intervene more wisely and more effectively in the real world to improve the well-being not only of yourself important as that may be but of people around you and of other species with whom we share the planet.
lines.cn: 它是让我们在现实世界中更明智、更有效地介入的手段，从而改善福祉——不仅是你自己的（尽管这也许很重要），还有你周围的人，以及与我们共享这个星球的其他物种的福祉。

lines.t: This is the end of listening comprehension.
lines.cn: 听力理解部分到此结束。
